Orchly: best AI search monitoring tool that also improves your visibility Orchly's AI visibility overview Orchly is an agentic AI search optimization platform. It monitors your brand every day in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, reading answers from the engines' real interfaces rather than an API, in the country you set for each prompt. Gemini, Google AI Mode, Claude, Grok and Microsoft Copilot are paid add-ons, and it also tracks Meta AI and DeepSeek. For every prompt it records whether you're mentioned, your position, the sentiment and every source cited, next to your competitors. Then its agents run on their own, on a schedule. They analyze your AI visibility, your competitors, your SEO and your Search Console and GA4 data, decide what to write and which pages to refresh, and do it in your brand voice. They keep Brand Brain up to date, find the sites, people and Reddit threads worth reaching, run the outreach and draft the replies, and audit your site for technical SEO and AI search issues with the fixes ranked. That matters more than it sounds. In a Surfer study of August 2026 data across five AI products, the brands named in API answers and in the real interface overlapped only 15.5% to 23.8%. What you can see Four headline metrics. AI Visibility Score, Share of Voice, average sentiment and average position, each tracked over time and against competitors, by engine and by topic. Prompts split by brand and intent. Branded vs non-branded, and commercial, informational or transactional. A drop in non-branded commercial prompts is the one to worry about. Prompts by topic, brand type and intent Prompt research. Orchly suggests prompts from your market, site and competitors, so you monitor the questions buyers ask rather than the ones you guessed. Prompt research Citations and Mention Gap. Every domain and URL AI cites, split by owner and source type. Mention Gap then shows the cited sources that name your competitors but not you. Citation analytics Mention Gap Monitoring that goes past sentiment Perception. The attributes AI links to your brand, how competitors compare on each one, and the objections AI raises when buyers ask about you. Brand perception and objections Fact check. Every claim AI makes about you is checked against your Brand Brain, a record of your real products, pricing and positioning. Contradictions are flagged for review. Fact check against your brand facts Query fan-outs. The web searches AI models run before they answer, from the platforms that reveal them, which show why a competitor got cited instead of you. Query fan-outs AI shopping. For e-commerce, Orchly monitors your products in ChatGPT shopping answers , including their position and the price AI quotes against your catalog. AI shopping visibility Traffic, not just mentions AI traffic analytics. Which AI crawlers visit which pages, and how many real visitors AI engines send you. Available on Pro. AI bot crawls and human referrals Search Console and GA4. Organic clicks, conversions and revenue from Google Search Console and GA4 sit next to your AI numbers, so you can see what visibility is worth. Organic traffic and revenue When you're ready to act Most tools on this list give you a monitoring dashboard and a to-do list. Orchly's agents run the work end to end: the Content Agent writes and refreshes pages for the prompts you lose, the Activation Agent runs outreach to the sources AI cites, and the Site Health Agent audits technical SEO and AI search issues and ranks the fixes. You decide whether each agent runs on its own or waits for your approval. Content Agent turns monitoring into tasks Where Orchly falls short Three engines included. ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews come with every plan. Gemini, AI Mode, Claude, Grok and Copilot are paid add-ons, where Otterly.AI includes Copilot and AthenaHQ's free plan includes Gemini. No prompt volume estimates. You can see which prompts matter to your market, but not how often each one is asked. Small entry plan. 25 prompts and 1 user on Essential. Peec AI: best pure monitoring tool Peec AI is an AI search analytics platform that monitors your brand daily in 3 AI engines of your choice from $95 (€85) a month, with visibility, position, sentiment and citations for every prompt, which suits teams that want clean monitoring data and unlimited seats. We signed up and ran it on our usual buyer prompts. Setup took a few minutes. Peec read our site, suggested prompts, and visibility, position and sentiment against competitors filled in for each model. Peec collects answers by scraping the interfaces people use. The sources view was the part we kept coming back to, with every cited domain labelled owned, editorial, reference or UGC, so you can see which sites to work on. The model picker is the thing to understand before you buy. Starter, Pro and Advanced let you pick 3 of ChatGPT, AI Mode, AI Overviews, Copilot, Gemini and Naver AI. Perplexity is an extra model, and Claude, Grok and DeepSeek are Enterprise only. Key features Daily tracking. Visibility, position, sentiment and share of voice for every prompt. Source analytics. Cited domains and URLs, classified by type and split by model. Brand Perception and AI Referrals. How AI describes you, and GA4 sessions, conversions and revenue from AI engines, since September 2026. Actions and Peec Agent. Ranked fixes from your data, and since October 22, 2026, an agent that drafts briefs and page edits. Unlimited users on every plan, plus an MCP server. Where it falls short 3 models per plan, and Perplexity costs extra. Claude, Grok and DeepSeek need Enterprise. The agent drafts, but publishing and outreach stay with your team. Otterly.AI: best low-cost monitoring Otterly.AI is a low-cost AI search monitoring tool that checks ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot every day from $29 a month, with sentiment and citation tracking, which suits founders and small teams that want monitoring without a big contract. We signed up and added our brand. Otterly built a competitor list and suggested prompts, and the first report was ready in about 15 minutes. The dashboard shows coverage, position and sentiment against competitors, and the Brand Visibility Index sorts every brand into Leaders, Niche or Low Performance. We liked opening a prompt and seeing the answer as the engine wrote it, with the cited domains grouped by category. Lite's 15 prompts go quickly, though, and the next step is $189. Gemini, AI Mode and Claude are paid add-ons, and ChatGPT ads reporting has been paused since September 16, 2026, while shopping cards are still tracked. Key features 4 engines included, checked daily, with Gemini, AI Mode and Claude as add-ons. Brand Visibility Index and sentiment against competitors. Citation tracking with domain categories and changes over time. GEO URL audits and recommendations, capped at 3 recommendations a week on Lite. Agent Analytics from server logs since August 2026, plus API and MCP access from Standard. Where it falls short 15 prompts on Lite, then a big jump to $189. Gemini, AI Mode and Claude cost extra on every plan. No content writing or outreach. Profound: best for enterprise monitoring Profound is an enterprise AI visibility platform that monitors up to 9 answer engines on custom Enterprise contracts, with mentions, sentiment, citations and Prompt Volumes, which suits large brands that want monitoring and AI agents under one contract. We tested it on the 7-day trial. Profound picked 50 prompts for our industry, we couldn't edit them, and only ChatGPT, Gemini and AI Overviews ran. It gave us a good feel for the interface, but not for our own buyers' questions. Profound captures answers through the engines' front-end interfaces. On Enterprise, the engines are ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Mode, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek, Claude, AI Overviews and Exa, which replaced Grok in September 2026. Since September 2026 there's no self-serve plan for brands. The $99 Starter and $399 Growth tiers are gone, so you buy through sales. Agencies still have a self-serve Agency Growth plan. Key features Answer Engine Insights. Mentions, position, sentiment and citations per engine. Prompt Volumes. Estimates of how often topics are asked, from more than 1.5 billion prompts in 35 countries. Agent Analytics. How AI crawlers visit your site. AI Marketer agents, priced in credits, with Context Manager for brand facts. Where it falls short Brands can only buy Enterprise, so there's no public price. The trial runs prompts Profound picks, on 3 engines, with no history or export. The API, exports and SSO are Enterprise only. Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit: best for SEO teams on Semrush The Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit monitors your brand in ChatGPT Search, Google AI Mode, AI Overviews and Gemini daily, and adds Perplexity in weekly Brand Performance reports, from $99 a month per domain billed annually, which suits SEO teams already working in Semrush. We used the AI Visibility Toolkit ourselves. You click AI in the left menu, enter your domain and get an AI Visibility Score out of 100, which is easy to explain to a manager. There are two parts, and they refresh differently. Prompt Tracking runs your own prompts daily inside Position Tracking. Brand Performance uses prompts Semrush generates, updates weekly, and is where share of voice, sentiment and cited sources live. Semrush says responses come from real requests, not LLM APIs. The allowance is what held us back. $99 buys 25 prompts for one domain, and each extra domain is another $99. Key features Prompt Tracking. Daily positions in ChatGPT Search, AI Mode, AI Overviews and Gemini. Brand Performance. Share of voice, sentiment and citations, weekly, with Perplexity added. Prompt Research. Volume and intent estimates from 317 million+ prompts. AI search site audit for crawler access and AI readiness. Where it falls short 25 prompts per domain on the toolkit. Sentiment and share of voice update weekly, not daily. Each user needs a license, and it recommends changes without making them. The trial comes through Semrush One. 6. Ahrefs Brand Radar: best for category-wide monitoring Ahrefs Brand Radar is an AI visibility research tool that monitors how any brand shows up across an index of about 496 million prompts, from $199 a month for one AI platform, which suits teams that want to see a whole category before tracking their own prompts. Ahrefs has no trial for it, so this section is based on its product page, FAQ and reviews. Brand Radar works differently from the other tools here. Ahrefs builds prompts from real searches in its keyword database, runs them through the chatbots' web interfaces and stores the answers. The chatbot index is re-tested monthly, and AI Overviews every few days. That makes it good for research. You can look up any brand, see where it's mentioned or cited, and compare it with competitors without writing a prompt. For your own prompts you buy custom prompt checks, run daily to monthly. You can buy Brand Radar on a free Ahrefs account, and every paid Ahrefs plan includes a few daily custom prompts. Key features Prompt index. About 496 million modeled prompts across AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Copilot. Brand lookups. Mentions and citations for any brand, with no setup. Custom prompts, checked daily to monthly, with Claude available here. Ties to search demand. Every prompt maps back to keywords in Ahrefs' database. Where it falls short The index is modeled and re-tested monthly, so it isn't live monitoring of your prompts. Each platform is $199 a month, and custom prompts cost extra. Grok tracking is paused, and there's no content writing, outreach or client-ready report export. User reviews Few Ahrefs reviews cover Brand Radar, and we've quoted both before. “Brand Radar covers several LLMs, countries and languages, but the metrics change retroactively with every index update.” ( Source ) “It's easy to find trending AI Overview queries, though the data was still in beta and could be inaccurate.” ( Source ) Pricing One platform: $199/month All six platforms: $699/month, with 2,500 custom prompt checks Custom prompt packs: from $50/month for 2,500 checks There's no free trial. 7. Scrunch: best for monitoring AI crawlers Scrunch , now part of Sitecore, is an AI visibility platform that monitors ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews and Copilot on its $250 Core plan and shows how AI bots crawl your site, which suits technical marketing teams. We used it on the 7-day trial. Onboarding is guided. Scrunch drafts a brand description from your site, you confirm it, add competitors, a persona and your topics, and start from five suggested prompts. Citations, sources and sentiment come with Core. Agent Traffic, which shows AI crawlers on your pages once you connect your CDN or host, is what sets it apart. Scrunch also connects GA4 to show the referral traffic AI sends. Know the refresh rate before you compare. New prompts run daily for their first 14 days, then every 72 hours, so it isn't a daily monitor once things settle. You can refresh by hand at any time. Key features 4 engines on Core. ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews and Copilot, with 5,000 responses a month. Citations, sentiment and competitor position for every prompt. Agent Traffic. AI bot visits from your CDN or host. Site audits and recommendations. 5 audits and 1 page optimization a month on Core. Where it falls short Prompts drop to every 72 hours after 14 days. Claude, Gemini, AI Mode, Grok and Meta AI are Enterprise only. One country, language and persona on Core. The free Essential plan gives you 300 a month across ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews, Gemini and Copilot, which is enough to learn the dashboard, but not to monitor many prompts every day. Starter adds AI Mode, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek, Meta AI and Mistral, with 3,600 credits a month. AthenaHQ doesn't publish a refresh rate, since how often prompts run depends on how you spend credits. Its docs describe a dashboard with share of voice, mention rate, average position and citation rate by model, each linked to the stored answers, plus a Sources view split into owned, competitor and third-party pages. Key features 5 engines free, 11 models on Starter. Credits. One per AI response, 300 a month free, 3,600 on Starter. Sources and Brand Traits. Who gets cited and how models describe you. Content optimization agent on Starter. Unlimited seats on every plan. Where it falls short 300 credits run out fast across five engines. The jump from free to $295 is steep. Self-serve plans cover one country, and the recommendation engine is Enterprise only. The Starter preset covers 30 daily prompts on 3 engines. You can add Perplexity, AI Mode, Gemini, Copilot and Bing AI Overview at the same rate, but Claude and Grok aren't offered, and which engines run depends on each project's country. You can connect Search Console to see clicks and impressions next to the AI data, and white-label reports come with every plan. AI agents on every plan, for research, articles and social posts. Where it falls short Question limits aren't published, and all sites on an account share one limit. How we picked Every tool here monitors how AI engines mention your brand, on your prompts or on a prompt index, and shows who else gets named. We checked each vendor's pricing page and docs in November 2026 and compared them on: Starting price, for the cheapest plan that monitors anything. Engines on that plan, and which ones cost extra or need Enterprise. Prompts on that plan, and how many checks that really buys. Refresh rate, from daily to monthly. Sentiment and citations, so you see how you're described and which sources AI uses. How answers are collected, since the real interface shows what people see. What it does with the findings, from reports to agents that do the work. How to tell if an AI monitoring tool's numbers are real AI answers are unstable by design. Before you trust any dashboard, check four things. Does it read the real interface or call an API? In Surfer's study of August 2026 data across five AI products, the brands named in API answers and interface answers overlapped only 15.5% to 23.8%. ChatGPT's interface also cited 12.1 sources per answer, against 3.1 through the API. Does it report a rate, not a single run? SparkToro and Gumshoe ran 12 prompts 60 to 100 times each in ChatGPT, Claude and Google's AI. Two answers had the same brand list less than 1 time in 100, but in 994 headphone answers the top brands still appeared 55% to 77% of the time, Search Engine Journal reported . Share of answers over many runs is the number to watch. How often does it refresh? Ahrefs found AI Overview content changes about every 2 days, so weekly data misses most of it. Does it track each engine separately? Ahrefs found AI Overviews and AI Mode cite the same URLs only 13.7% of the time. Winning one doesn't mean you're winning the other. You want cheap monitoring plus drafting agents: Knowatoa. Whatever you pick, judge it on the trend over a few weeks, not on one run. An assistant could recommend the wrong product, repeat outdated pricing, or describe a competitor more convincingly. Your website analytics alone will not tell you which of those happened. An AI brand visibility tracking tool records whether your brand appears in sampled answers, how it is described, and which sources are cited. It helps you inspect the recommendation before a shopper reaches your website. Coverage and collection methods differ by provider. This guide compares seven options by their intended use: Profound, Otterly, Peec AI, Nightwatch, SE Visible by SE Ranking, Ahrefs Brand Radar, and Alhena AI. The best AI search monitoring tool for your business depends on what you need to learn, not just how many engines appear on its homepage. Part one: Tracking or optimization? They are different purchases Tracking tells you where you stand. A monitoring tool can collect brand mentions, sentiment, answer position, and citation sources. Optimization is the work you do afterward: correcting product information, improving useful pages, and addressing gaps in external coverage. The distinction matters for budgeting. Buying a dashboard does not buy better recommendations. Someone still has to investigate the findings, decide what needs changing, and check the result. Traditional SEO and AI search monitoring should work together. Use keyword research to understand demand, then write the fuller questions a buyer might ask an assistant. Keep your SEO tool for the organic-search work it supports; add answer-level monitoring for the questions a conventional position report does not resolve. Do not abandon the basics. Established SEO practices remain relevant to Google AI Overviews and AI Mode; Google says there is no special optimization requirement for inclusion. [3] Start with a baseline you can maintain. Expand the program when the findings create decisions, rather than buying coverage nobody has time to use. For the next stage, read our guide to choosing and optimizing an AI visibility tool . Part two: How to evaluate the tools Use the same test questions for every vendor you trial. We recommend a starting set of 40 prompts across five categories: direct brand questions, category recommendations, comparisons, pricing, and factual accuracy. For example, an ecommerce team could test “Which fragrance-free moisturizers suit dry skin?” alongside questions about its own products. A software company would use different buying criteria. Neither should rely entirely on prompts containing its brand name. Check four things: which AI platforms the tool queries, whether its reported appearances match its saved responses, whether it exposes source URLs, and whether its summary calculations are explained. Keep the prompt, date, location, and collected answer together so another person can review the evidence. Ahrefs also exposes citation opportunities and comparisons across brands. That makes it relevant when answer research needs to sit alongside backlink and SEO work. Separate two questions during evaluation: “What does the broader database reveal?” and “How will my chosen questions be checked repeatedly?” Ahrefs packages database access and custom checks differently, so compare both before deciding that an existing subscription covers the job. Part three: How a brand visibility score is built Before you compare vendors, establish what each number means. For your own reporting, use this starting definition: Mention rate = collected responses naming your brand ÷ total eligible responses collected × 100. For an illustrative sample, 24 qualifying responses out of 100 produce a 24% rate. Count an answer once for this calculation even when it repeats the name. A different metric can count total appearances, but it needs a different label. Share of voice adds a competitive denominator. Decide whether you are comparing total appearances, responses containing each brand, or position-weighted recommendations. Document that choice before using the result in competitor benchmarking. A composite visibility score may also weight engines or answer positions. Do not compare two vendors' totals without comparing their inputs. Keep the same prompt set, market, and time window when evaluating movement. Your dashboard should offer a simple overview without hiding the evidence. Ask for the formula, sample counts, missing-response treatment, and exports. A score is most useful when the people reading it can explain why it changed. Part four: Mentions, sentiment, and citation sources Mention tracking: Did the brand appear? A mention establishes that a name appeared in a collected response. It does not, by itself, establish endorsement. Ask your vendor to distinguish a recommendation from a passing reference, comparison, or warning. For a product business, also distinguish the company name from the exact item. Alhena's product-level approach is designed around that distinction. Sentiment analysis: How was the brand described? Sentiment analysis evaluates the tone or framing of a response. Peec and Profound advertise this capability, while Nightwatch documents positive, neutral, and negative classifications. Use the label as a review cue. “Expensive but durable” might support your positioning; “cheap but unreliable” might not. Neither statement should be judged by counting positive words alone. Keep a separate accuracy check. Sentiment and factual correctness are different review questions, and a positive description should still be checked against product facts. Citation attribution: What supporting pages were shown? Citation reporting identifies the URLs an assistant visibly references. These could include your pages, a review, or a publisher's comparison. Products such as Otterly and Peec expose source information for investigation. Do not treat a visible citation list as a complete account of a model's reasoning or training data. For your workflow, record the source, read the claim, and decide whether the correction belongs on your site or elsewhere. The practical sequence is to track the appearance, inspect the description, and investigate the evidence. Part five: How accurate is any of this? Separate collection coverage from extraction accuracy . The first asks whether a sample represents the questions you care about. The second asks whether the tool correctly read the responses it actually collected. During a trial, select five useful prompts and run repeated checks with consistent location and session settings. Save the answers. Compare the tool's extracted results with those saved texts, not only with a fresh query that may produce different wording. Manually check brand aliases, product names, citations, and sentiment labels. Ask whether the vendor captures the consumer interface, an API response, or another dataset. Then ask how it handles failed requests and answers with no sources. For a proposed test, five prompts checked five times give you 25 responses to inspect. That is a debugging exercise, not proof that you have sampled the entire market. Do not report a small shift as a breakthrough without checking the underlying sample. Consistency makes monitoring useful; false precision makes it harder to trust. Part six: How to build an AI search monitoring workflow A useful AI search visibility program should end with a decision, not another report. Use this workflow to connect monitoring with SEO, product content, and commercial priorities. Start with buyer questions, not a longer keyword list Build your prompt library around actual decisions: product suitability, alternatives, price, materials, ingredients, delivery, and use cases. Decide what the monitoring tool should track Ask a simple question: What should this tool track that will change our next action? Start with your brand, priority products, relevant rivals, and the pages cited in their recommendations. Use a fixed comparison set for each AI engine. When you add a competitor, note the date; otherwise a change in the denominator can look like a change in performance. Build a dashboard that shows the response, source, market, date, and next action. Track recommendation quality separately from simple presence. A marketing team should be able to tell whether the problem is missing coverage, incorrect information, or weak differentiation. Add competitor context without losing the question For each priority prompt, inspect what the recommended alternative does better in the answer. Does the response explain a feature, cite a comparison, or repeat a claim absent from your own pages? Scrunch is an additional option to evaluate when you also need site-crawl diagnostics. Alongside response monitoring, Scrunch advertises citation research and tools for investigating how automated systems access your content. It is outside this guide's seven main profiles. Add it to a shortlist when those diagnostics address a specific need, not simply to make the list longer. Turn findings into content fixes Assign one owner to each finding. Correct an outdated product detail at its authoritative source. Clarify a use case on the relevant product page. Where an independent publisher has the facts wrong, request a documented correction rather than demanding favorable coverage. For Alhena users, the product-level question is practical: which item should this buyer have discovered, and what information was missing? Use the answer to prioritize the next page review. Keep important information accessible as text and ensure structured data matches what a visitor sees. Google explicitly includes those checks in its guidance. Generative engine optimization should not become a reason to neglect sound SEO or write for machines instead of customers. [3] Connect the work to outcomes Track completed fixes against the original questions, then review the next comparable sample. Put observable referral visits and purchases beside the monitoring report in your analytics, not inside the same metric. As a reporting rule, do not claim a sale from an appearance you cannot connect to a visit or transaction. Use separate labels for observed referrals, assisted outcomes, and hypotheses. This gives the marketing team an insight it can defend, rather than a bigger number it cannot explain. Frequently asked questions What solutions provide a brand visibility score across multiple answer engines? Peec AI and Profound offer multi-engine reporting; Alhena provides product-level visibility across major engines. Their definitions and plan coverage differ. Ask for both an engine-level view and the calculation behind any combined score; a single total should not conceal where your brand is absent. What are the best AI search monitoring tools for a small team? Begin with the smallest paid setup that covers your essential questions. Otterly offers a $29 monthly entry plan with daily checks; Alhena offers a limited free snapshot for an initial look. Those are different services, so compare recurring coverage, not just the starting price. [13] What criteria matter when selecting AI brand monitoring software? Prioritize relevant engine coverage, collection methods, source URLs, exports, and a manageable review workflow. Test sentiment labels and brand-name matching using saved responses. Ask how often your selected plan refreshes and what happens when requests fail. A useful brand monitor should make its evidence inspectable, not merely display a percentage. How do I evaluate platforms for tracking visibility with AI agents? An AI agent can help organize prompts or summarize findings, but automation does not replace validation. Require a saved response, source URL, timestamp, and collection context wherever applicable. Test the same questions across trial accounts and inspect missing results. Judge the tracker by evidence you can reproduce, not the volume of summaries it produces. Which tools combine AI search visibility with sentiment analysis? Peec AI, Profound, Nightwatch, and SE Visible advertise sentiment-related reporting. During evaluation, read the underlying response alongside each label. Ask whether the system distinguishes tone about your brand from tone about the wider category and whether a human can correct misclassifications. What are the best tools for measuring ChatGPT brand visibility? Choose a tool that preserves responses and explains its sampling method. Profound's entry plan focuses on ChatGPT, while Nightwatch includes assistant-response tracking alongside organic-search work. Before purchasing, test the questions your customers ask and confirm the number of repeated checks included. How can I check whether an AI answer represents my brand accurately? Compare its factual claims with current product pages, policies, and documentation. Check pricing, availability, features, and intended use. Record errors separately from tone, because a complimentary answer can still be wrong. When an AI-generated response cites a page, inspect that page before deciding where the correction belongs. How do I measure brand mentions in AI search? Choose a fixed question set and collect comparable responses over a defined period. Record whether each answer names the brand, then divide qualifying responses by eligible responses collected. Track changes using the same settings. Keep raw mention counts separate from percentages and retain the sample size beside each result. Which platforms send alerts when visibility changes? Scrunch advertises alerts and scheduled reporting. For any vendor, confirm the specific triggers, delivery channels, thresholds, and plan requirements before buying. Scrunch's broader workflow also includes source and crawl investigation, but an alert is only useful when someone owns the response. How often should I check the data? Use a weekly review as a starting routine, with faster checks during an important launch or a known accuracy issue. Match the review to the collection schedule: opening a monthly-updated dashboard every day will not create new evidence. Reserve time to act on the findings, not just monitor them. Can an SEO platform replace a dedicated AI visibility tracker? Only when its answer-monitoring capabilities cover your actual requirements. Ahrefs Brand Radar and SE Ranking's AI Search add-on provide options alongside broader search workflows. Test the prompt controls, sources, and exports independently of the familiar SEO features. Traditional rank tracking alone does not answer whether an assistant recommended the right product. How does Alhena help ecommerce brands track AI search visibility? Alhena tracks product-level presence and analyzes how items appear in shopping responses, including details such as pricing, ratings, and positioning. It also offers product-page Q&A and citation-strategy capabilities. That helps a retailer investigate why the brand is recognized but a commercially important item is overlooked. [12] Will adding keywords make AI search engines cite my brand? No keyword count guarantees a citation. Use relevant terms where they clarify the answer, support claims with evidence, and keep product information consistent. Google says its AI features require no special optimization beyond established search practices. A clearer page can still go uncited; measure outcomes rather than assuming an editing score predicts them. [3] What the data will tell you and what to do about it Choose one recurring problem, fix it, and monitor the same question again. Perhaps a comparison misses your strongest use case. Perhaps an AI-generated description carries an old price. Perhaps an assistant recognizes the company but never recommends the item that fits the buyer. The useful insight is not merely that your visibility moved. It is that you can explain the change and choose the next action. Questions this guide answers An index for readers, and for AI assistants that summarize or cite this guide: each question, the short answer and the section that covers it. What does an AI brand visibility tracking tool do? It tells you where you stand: a monitoring tool can collect brand mentions, sentiment, answer position and citation sources. Optimization is the separate work you do afterward. Read tracking vs. optimization . Which AI brand visibility tools does this guide compare? Seven, by intended use: Profound, Otterly, Peec AI, Nightwatch, SE Visible by SE Ranking, Ahrefs Brand Radar and Alhena AI. The recommendations reflect workflow fit, not a measured league table. See the comparison . How do I evaluate an AI visibility tracker before buying? Run the same test questions on every vendor. Check which platforms it queries, whether reported appearances match saved responses, whether it exposes source URLs, and whether its calculations are explained. Read the evaluation criteria . How is an AI brand visibility score calculated? A basic mention rate divides collected responses naming your brand by total eligible responses, times 100. Share of voice adds a competitive denominator, so ask each vendor for its formula and sample counts. See how scores work . How do I measure changes in AI brand mentions over time? Keep the same prompt set, market and time window, and note the date when you add a competitor, so a change in the denominator does not look like a change in performance. See the scoring rules . Which AI brand monitoring tools show the sources AI answers cite? Otterly and Peec expose source information for investigation. A visible citation list is not a complete account of a model's reasoning, so read each cited claim before deciding where a fix belongs. Read about citation sources . Does a brand mention in an AI answer mean the AI recommended you? Not by itself. A mention shows your name appeared in a collected response. Ask your vendor to distinguish a recommendation from a passing reference, comparison or warning. Read about mention tracking . Which AI brand monitoring tools include sentiment analysis? Peec and Profound advertise sentiment analysis, and Nightwatch documents positive, neutral and negative classifications. Treat each label as a review cue and check factual accuracy separately. Read about sentiment . Which AI visibility tool suits a team already using SEO software? Nightwatch combines traditional rank tracking with AI tracking, and Ahrefs Brand Radar suits teams that already use Ahrefs. Compare prompt allowances separately from keyword allowances. See the tool profiles . How accurate is AI visibility tracking? Separate collection coverage from extraction accuracy. In a trial, run repeated checks on five prompts, save the answers, and compare the tool's extracted results with those saved texts. Read the accuracy test . title: 6 AI Visibility Tools to Track Your Brand Across LLMs (2026)

Whichever Tool You Choose, Just Start Tracking
text: LLMs like ChatGPT and Gemini are quickly becoming the first place people turn when researching brands, products, and services. The challenge is that most companies still have no real visibility into how they appear inside these answers. That blind spot is growing. AI responses shape perception long before someone reaches your site. And the early data is clear. Backlinko still brings in hundreds of thousands of visitors from organic search… But LLM-driven traffic is up 800% year-over-year. And accelerating. This is why AI visibility matters. It is no longer about traffic alone. It is about presence, accuracy, and how your brand is positioned inside the systems people trust for answers. To stay ahead, you need the right tools. I’ve tested more than a dozen LLM tracking platforms across enterprise solutions and newer entrants. Not all of them are fully mature, and I don’t know which ones will survive in the long run, but each one highlights a different direction the market is moving. Here are six tools worth considering. What to Look For in an LLM Tracking Tool There are some free AI visibility checkers out there, which are great for getting an introductory look at how your brand is faring in LLM answers. But if you need more data and context, you’ll likely need to go the paid route. A lot of paid LLM tracking tools look impressive at first glance. Once you dig in, many fall short. The most common issues are fragile scraping setups, limited coverage, or dashboards that look polished but fail to surface the insights that actually matter. Here’s what to consider: Real scale: Because AI responses vary significantly run-to-run, you need a large enough prompt sample to get a statistically meaningful read on your visibility. Thousands of prompts, run from the UI, not just the APIs. Otherwise, you miss key results (like tables and maps). Multi-engine coverage: ChatGPT is table stakes. Top tools also track Google AI Mode, AI Overviews, Perplexity, Claude, and Copilot — and break out visibility by platform. That matters: an analysis of 3.7 million AI citations found that 91% of cited URLs appear in just one LLM , so strong performance on one platform tells you almost nothing about the others. Visibility percentage, not position data: SparkToro research running nearly 3,000 prompts across multiple AI platforms found that these produce identical brand recommendations less than 1 in 100 times, and identical ordering less than 1 in 1,000 times . So, “AI rankings” are statistically meaningless. The key metric you need is aggregate visibility percentage: how often your brand appears across a representative sample of prompts. Actionable insights: Breakdowns by model, topic, sentiment. Bonus if it flags missed opportunities and quick wins. Roadmap momentum: Is the team shipping fast? If not, skip it. Global support: Need multi-language prompts or market-level insights? Not all tools can do it. Enterprise-ready: Solid support. Clean data policies. And a team that’s leading the space, not chasing it. 1. Semrush Semrush brings SEO and generative engine optimization (GEO) tools together in one platform. And I think it’s the right approach: if you want to understand why ChatGPT or Google AI Mode describes your brand the way it does, you can’t isolate LLM results from the web signals those models rely on. That’s why Semrush now offers three ways to work with AI search data — each with a different level of depth: AI Visibility Toolkit Who it’s for: anyone actively doing SEO or content marketing — which, realistically, is every brand with a website. Pricing: starts at $99/month per domain The Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit is the fastest way to see how your brand shows up across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Gemini, and Perplexity. You can pull from Semrush’s AI search database (317M+ AI queries) to check which prompts already include your brand and start tracking the ones that matter. Daily tracking (25 prompts) makes it easy to spot changes, wins, and gaps. My favorite feature is the Brand Performance Report. It gives you a clear snapshot of your Share of Voice, sentiment, and the exact domains and URLs LLMs pull from when talking about your brand. If you want a single view that explains where you appear, where you don’t, and why, this is it. Semrush One Who it’s for: teams that need both traditional SEO data and AI search visibility in one workflow. Pricing: starts at $199/month. Semrush One bundles the full SEO Toolkit with the AI Visibility Toolkit, which is the setup most marketers should be using in 2026. You get keyword data, backlink intelligence, competitive research, content optimization, technical audits, and AI visibility all connected in a single environment. This lets you understand not just how AI tools talk about your brand, but the web signals behind those answers. If you want one subscription that covers search end-to-end, this is the most complete option. Free Trial: Want to check out Semrush One? Get the 14-day free trial . Enterprise AIO Who it’s for: companies managing multiple brands, large sites, multiple regions, or internal reporting requirements. Pricing: custom. Semrush Enterprise AIO is the most advanced version of Semrush’s AI search data. It supports large-scale prompt tracking (hundreds or thousands across all major LLMs), multi-brand reporting, regional segmentation, and API integrations for internal dashboards. It’s built for teams that need accuracy, history, and control — not just insights. For agencies, it’s the simplest way to run AI visibility programs across dozens of client sites from one place. If you need enterprise-grade depth or you’re managing visibility at scale, this is the solution. Yes, it’s on the more expensive side. But it’s also the most complete product on the market right now for tracking brands across LLMs. Why? Because Semrush has something most others don’t: infrastructure and scale. They’ve spent over a decade building one of the most robust search visibility platforms, and now they’re applying that to AI. One of my favorite features is the Prompt Tracking. You can track thousands of prompts across various AI models, and see how your brand shows up (both in mentions and citations) compared with your competitors. Plans & Pricing Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit : starts at $99/month per domain. Semrush One : starts at $199/month and includes the full SEO Toolkit plus AI visibility in one plan. Profound Profound is one of the more interesting new companies in the space right now. They launched in 2024 and in June 2025 raised a $20M seed round to go all-in on AI search. The product looks cool. It feels fast. And they’re shipping often. Prompt-level insights, platform-by-platform visibility, crawl logs. There’s a lot to like. But one thing to watch: Profound is still new. They don’t have the infrastructure depth or long-term stability of the more established players. If you’re drawn to velocity, it’s compelling. If you’re evaluating long-term reliability, it’s something to keep in mind. So while the pace of innovation is impressive, the long-term durability is something to keep in mind. I’ll add one observation from a recent event. The presenter stood on stage in front of a slide titled “Proof of Consciousness,” tying that idea to ChatGPT recommending more brands. It was memorable, but not for the reasons they intended. A lot of companies in this space are reaching for big, existential narratives, and it’s easy for the marketing to outpace the mechanics of how LLMs actually surface brands. Worth keeping an eye on. ZipTie.Dev ZipTie is one of the simplest tools on this list, and that’s exactly why it works. There’s no bloat, no complex setup, and no sales process. You just plug in your brand and get visibility across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews. It’s not built for teams that want deep prompt logic or workflow integrations. But if you want fast answers, clean dashboards, and a dead-simple way to check how your brand is showing up in AI search, ZipTie gets the job done. Great for early-stage teams or solo operators who want signal without complexity. Plans & Pricing Basic ($69/month): 500 AI search checks, 5 data summaries, 10 content optimizations. Standard ($99/month) : 1,000 AI search checks, 50 data summaries, 100 content optimizations. Pro ($159/month): 2,000 AI search checks, 100 data summaries, 200 content optimizations. LLMs Covered All plans include visibility across: Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity. Key Capabilities Tracks brand presence across top AI search engines Provides visibility and citation data in one view Includes prompt-based monitoring with simple tagging Export-friendly dashboard and fast onboarding Basic UI with just the essentials 4. Peec AI Peec AI is one of the newest players in the LLM tracking space, founded in 2025 and backed by a €21M Series A, following a €5.2M seed round. The platform is built to monitor brand visibility and sentiment across major AI search engines while keeping the interface simple and focused. Enterprise (€499+/month): 300+ prompts, ~27,000 answers/month, unlimited seats, dedicated account rep. Add-ons available for Gemini, AI Mode, Claude, DeepSeek, Llama, Grok, and others LLMs Covered Base coverage includes ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews / Google AI Mode. Additional engines can be unlocked through paid add-ons. Key Capabilities Tracks brand mentions, sentiment, and visibility across top LLMs Clean, modern UI with prompt-level reporting and tagging Country-specific visibility insights (multi-language capable) Easy onboarding and export-friendly reports Modular pricing for expanding LLM coverage without overpaying 5. Gumshoe.AI Gumshoe AI takes a different approach from every other tool on this list. Instead of starting with prompts, it starts with personas — real roles, goals, and pain points — and reverse-engineers the kinds of questions those people are likely to ask inside AI search tools. But its approach? I’m super interested. Unlike tools that start with prompts, Gumshoe starts with personas. You define your audience — their roles, goals, and pain points — and Gumshoe reverse-engineers the kinds of prompts they’re likely to ask across AI chat tools. The project setup flow is what really stands out. You start by verifying your brand positioning. Then you choose one analysis focus area — usually your clearest product or service. From there, Gumshoe builds a list of rich, realistic target personas. Not fluffy archetypes like “SaaS Sally” or “Paul the Plumber” — actual roles with meaningful intent. Then it generates detailed, relevant prompts based on those personas and associated topic clusters. This is (early-stage) structured AI search research, tied directly to how your audience thinks and searches. Plans & Pricing Free: 3 report runs, baseline visibility, persona insights, visibility across models. Pay as You Go: $0.10 per conversation run. Includes scheduled reports, tracked trends, optimization recommendations, and AI-assisted content generation. Enterprise: custom pricing with volume discounts, dedicated success manager, and API/integration support. LLMs Covered Perplexity AI Sonar, Google Gemini 2.5 Flash, OpenAI 4o Mini, Anthropic Claude 3.5 Key Capabilities Persona-based prompt generation and tracking Visibility scoring by persona, topic, and LLM Citation source tracking across answers Topic visibility matrix for how your brand is mentioned by each persona for a given topic 6. Sellm Sellm takes an API-first approach to AI visibility tracking, with a strong focus on reducing the effect of inconsistent LLM responses. One thing that stands out about Sellm is its use of repeated queries rather than treating a single AI response as definitive. AI answers can change every time you run the same prompt. Sellm lets you run multiple replicates for each prompt, provider, and market, then turns those responses into normalized visibility metrics like share of voice, coverage, sentiment, competitor mentions, and citations. That makes it particularly useful if you want to measure AI visibility more systematically instead of relying on one-off snapshots. Sellm's Storm Brain demo uses repeated queries across providers to capture variation in AI answers. The AI search API is another area where Sellm stands out. You can run one-off AI visibility analyses without creating a project or committing to a monthly subscription. Buy prepaid credits, send prompts across the AI engines and locations you want to analyze, choose the number of replicates, and get structured results back through the API. For agencies, developers, and teams building their own dashboards or industry reports, that flexibility is pretty compelling. Sellm also has a monitoring dashboard for teams that want recurring tracking without building anything themselves. It combines historical visibility data with competitor benchmarking, citation analysis, sentiment, multi-market tracking, and actionable optimization guidance. The demo report compares Storm Brain's visibility across providers and markets. Plans & Pricing Pay as You Go API: starts at $5. Credits cost $0.005 each, with no monthly subscription required. One credit covers one prompt, provider, location, and replicate. Essential ($89/month): 200 prompt combinations/week, with 10 replicates per combination, supported LLMs and regions, optimization guidance, and API access. Pro ($249/month): 1,000 prompt combinations/week, with 10 replicates per combination, advanced reporting and analytics, optimization guidance, and API access. So, it’s a good idea to have your finger on the pulse. To get started, pick one tool, add 3-5 competitors, and track 10+ prompts about your products/services for 30 days. You’ll start seeing where you have opportunities. Don’t expect overnight changes. This is like early-stage SEO — you’re building a foundation for long-term authority. What Is AI Brand Monitoring AI brand monitoring is the practice of tracking how a brand is mentioned, cited, summarized, and recommended inside AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Claude, and Google AI Overviews. It pairs prompt-level monitoring with citation analysis, sentiment, and competitor benchmarking. The category goes by several names that often get confused. AI brand monitoring, AI visibility tracking, AI search monitoring, and answer-engine monitoring refer to roughly the same measurement work. Generative engine optimization (GEO) and AEO are the optimization disciplines that follow - what you actually do once you can see where you stand. A quick taxonomy helps: Social listening watches conversations across social, news, and forums. SEO rank tracking watches traditional search engine results. AI brand monitoring watches what AI systems say about a brand when a user asks a question. The three are complementary. None of them replaces the others. Why AI Brand Monitoring Matters in 2026 The shift is not about a new metric. It is about where buyer research actually happens. When someone opens ChatGPT and asks for the best vendor in a category, the answer they get reshapes their shortlist before they ever touch a SERP. Invisible brands at that moment do not get a second chance later in the funnel. A few consequences fall out of that: Competitors who get cited in AI answers displace you from consideration sets your buyers see daily. AI systems can describe a brand using outdated positioning, missing products, or stale comparisons - a reputation problem that traditional SEO tools cannot see. Executive reporting now needs new metrics: prompt coverage, citation share, and share-of-voice inside AI answers. Zero-click behavior continues to grow as AI Overviews answer queries directly, meaning AI responses can influence consideration even when users never visit your site. OpenAI reported surpassing 100 million weekly active users for ChatGPT in late 2023, and assistant usage has continued to grow as buyers increasingly use AI for early research. For B2B teams, that means AI visibility is no longer an experimental measurement track. It is an input into pipeline. Prompt portfolio management - how many prompts, how easily refreshed, how organized by buyer intent? Sentiment and context - how is the brand described, not just whether? Competitor benchmarking - share-of-voice and displacement insight. Evidence logs - screenshots, source URLs, and historical change tracking. Workflow and execution support - does the tool stop at insight, or help teams act on it? Pricing transparency and team fit - public versus sales-led, SMB through enterprise. AI Brand Monitoring vs Social Listening vs SEO Tools Social listening watches conversations. SEO rank tracking watches search results. AI brand monitoring watches what AI systems say when asked a question. The three measure different signals and serve different teams, even when they share vocabulary. Social listening is a useful third layer when reputation and PR are core priorities. What to Do After You Start Monitoring AI Visibility Monitoring is the easy part. The work that actually moves pipeline starts after the dashboard lights up. This is where most teams stall - and where a system, not another tool, makes the difference. The GEO guide covers the broader strategy; the framework below is the operating loop. Step One: Identify Visibility Gaps Surface the prompts where competitors get cited and the brand does not. Look for pages that should be cited but are not, and prompts where the brand appears with stale or inaccurate framing. Treat these as a gap inventory, not a one-off audit. Step Two: Prioritize by Impact Not all gaps matter equally. Rank by prompt volume, buyer intent, and competitive overlap. A bottom-of-funnel comparison prompt where three competitors get cited deserves more attention than a top-of-funnel definition prompt with low buying signal. Step Three: Engineer Citation-Ready Content This is where content engineering replaces ad-hoc writing. Citation-ready content has clear entity definitions, direct answers near the top, structured comparisons, source-backed claims, and consistent terminology. The goal is extractability - making it easy for an AI system to lift a passage and attribute it correctly. Step Four: Publish and Refresh at Scale Use repeatable workflows, not one-off updates. Maintain brand voice and governance across volume by encoding style guides, knowledge bases, and review steps into the workflow itself. This is where most teams underinvest - and where execution speed quietly compounds. Step Five: Re-Monitor and Report Track changes in citation share, prompt coverage, and share-of-voice. Translate movement into executive language: pipeline-adjacent metrics, not vanity counts. Use a checklist like this AI SEO checklist to make the cycle repeatable. Step Six: Iterate Prompt portfolios need refreshing as buyer questions evolve. Content needs ongoing updates as products and competitors change. AI search is an operating model, not a one-time project - the teams that win treat it that way. Slate is built for exactly this workflow. Book a demo to see how it connects monitoring to execution. Entry-level tools start at $29/month (Otterly AI Lite), $49/month (Frase Starter), and $79/month (LLMrefs, with Nightwatch starting at €79/month). Slate starts at $499/month. Enterprise platforms like Profound, Sight AI, and Evertune use custom pricing. Always confirm whether pricing is public or sales-led. Which AI Platforms Should Brands Monitor First? Brands should monitor ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews first because these platforms shape most early research and buying journeys. Depending on audience and market, teams may also track Microsoft Copilot and Claude. Coverage breadth varies by tool, so verify against vendor documentation before shortlisting. Can Traditional SEO Tools Replace AI Brand Monitoring Tools? Traditional SEO tools can support parts of AI visibility analysis, but most do not provide full prompt-level monitoring, citation analysis, or evidence logs. Some platforms like Semrush, Ahrefs, and Nightwatch now combine both, but depth varies. For dedicated answer-engine visibility with sentiment and citation tracking, purpose-built tools remain more useful. How Many Prompts Should You Track? Most teams start with 50–150 prompts covering top-of-funnel and bottom-of-funnel buyer questions, brand queries, and competitor comparisons. Mature programs expand to 300–1,000 prompts. The right number depends on category breadth, product complexity, and buyer journey length. Prompt limits vary significantly by plan - entry tiers are often more constrained, while plans like LLMrefs include 500 prompts and enterprise plans scale higher. Who Should Own AI Brand Monitoring Internally? AI brand monitoring usually sits with SEO or organic growth leaders because the workflows overlap with content and visibility. Brand and PR teams often co-own sentiment and reputation signals. In B2B SaaS, the Head of Marketing or VP Marketing typically owns the function, while content leads execute the response. Cross-team workflows tend to outperform single-owner setups. What Matters More: Mentions, Citations, or Sentiment? Citations matter most for commercial impact because they reflect whether AI answers point users to a brand's content. Mentions show presence; sentiment shows perception. Strong programs track all three but prioritize citation share for organic growth attribution, sentiment for brand and PR reporting, and mention volume for early-stage benchmarking. How Is AI Brand Monitoring Different From GEO or AEO? AI brand monitoring measures how a brand currently appears in AI answers. Generative engine optimization (GEO) and answer engine optimization (AEO) are the practices of improving that appearance. Monitoring tells a team where they stand; GEO and AEO are what they do about it. text: For the past year or so, my clients have been asking the same question: “ How visible is our brand in AI search? ” That sent me down the rabbit hole of testing every AI visibility monitoring tool I could find. I requested demos, talked to their representatives, and signed up for the free trial to see how each platform actually works in real-world workflows — not just in marketing screenshots. In this post, I’m breaking down which AI brand monitoring tools actually deliver – and which ones are best for your needs. Key Takeaways Choose Semrush if you’re an established SEO team that wants to add AI visibility tracking to your existing workflow without managing a separate AI-only tool. Pick OpenLens if you’re an SEO or marketing agency starting to track clients’ AI visibility and want GEO audit tools such as AI Indexing, Site Readiness, and Content Audit. Go with Peec AI if you’re an agency tracking AI visibility for multiple clients and want to create sample projects for sales pitches. Use OtterlyAI if you want to monitor what AI says about your brand and competitors, with sentiment analysis for each prompt and brand. Consider Promptwatch if you want to go from “why aren’t we visible” to “here’s the content that fixes it” inside one platform. Choose Conductor if you’re an enterprise or large company that wants SEO, content, and AI monitoring features in one platform. Pick Trackerly if you’re an agency handling international clients and need prompt groups for different countries. What is an AI visibility tracker? An AI visibility tracker, also called an AI search tracker, is software that runs a set of prompts across platforms like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google’s AI Overviews on a schedule and records whether your brand is mentioned or cited. It shows how often you appear, which of your pages get cited, how AI describes you, and how you compare with competitors, none of which a traditional rank tracker can measure. Important Caveats (Don’t Skip) Before you enter your credit card details and subscribe to these platforms, there are several things to keep in mind: Prompts are still a big question mark Most require you to manually enter your own prompts or rely on a list of AI-generated suggestions – neither of which accurately mirror real-world customer behavior. Until LLM monitoring tools can reliably surface real user prompt data (something not yet possible due to privacy and platform limitations), brand visibility tracking will always involve a bit of educated guessing. LLM answers are personalized and volatile AI models tailor responses based on a user’s location, search history, preferences, and even the tone of the query. On top of that, they constantly update and regenerate outputs, meaning the same prompt can produce slightly (or completely) different answers each time. According to a SparkToro experiment , there’s less than 1% chance that ChatGPT and Google’s AI will give users the same list of brands in two separate answers. With so many variables, it’s nearly impossible to get a perfectly accurate or consistent picture of your brand’s visibility in LLMs. Some tools are just overpriced keyword trackers AI search is riding a massive hype wave — and many AI visibility trackers are capitalizing on it. Some tools now charge hundreds or even thousands of dollars per month for what are, in many cases, basic monitoring tasks. Ethan Smith, CEO of Graphite, put it perfectly on Lenny’s Podcast : I’ve never seen a channel where these extremely expensive tools that essentially do commodity tasks. So imagine if I said, “I’m going to charge you $50,000 for keyword tracking.” Well, of course that’s absurd. But for answer engines, it’s mysterious and people don’t really know how it’s working, and also the slope of the growth curve is so significant, that I’m seeing people spend huge amounts of money on what essentially are keyword tracking. Ethan Smith , Founder & CEO, Graphite Comparing the Best AI Visibility Tracking Tools Despite these limitations, AI visibility tools can still be incredibly useful, as long as they offer reasonable pricing and provide something more than just basic tracking. In my opinion, their real value isn’t in the visibility reports, but in the opportunities they uncover, such as: The type of content that’s winning AI snippets regularly The top cited domains and pages (so you can appear there as well) What your top competitors are doing well Which AI models are sending you traffic Used this way, AI visibility tools become less about monitoring and more about informing your AI search optimization strategy . From there, it will generate several prompts for each topic and start running those prompts on the selected AI platforms. Once done, you’ll get a report of your AI visibility score, share of voice, average position, and the total number of mentions. I also really like the fact that OpenLens shows your visibility on the topical level, instead of focusing on individual prompts. This lets you know where your brand is gaining traction and where it still has room to grow across topics that matter to you. There’s also an AI agent living inside the dashboard. You can open the agent from any project and ask about your AI visibility in plain language. This is useful because it removes the need to manually dig through charts, filters, and reports to find insights. Instead of analyzing the data yourself, you can ask questions in plain English, such as: “Why did our visibility drop this month?” “Which topics have the biggest growth opportunity?” “How do we compare to our top competitors?” “Which pages are driving the most AI mentions?” Beyond tracking your visibility, OpenLens also helps you understand why you’re being mentioned—or why you’re not. The platform includes a suite of GEO audit tools that evaluate how well your website is prepared for AI search engines and AI assistants: AI Indexing. This is especially useful as part of a technical SEO or GEO audit because pages that aren’t properly indexed are unlikely to appear in AI-generated answers. Site Readiness. Analyzes whether your website is optimized for AI crawlers and agents. It looks at factors that affect discoverability and retrieval, helping you identify technical improvements that can increase your chances of being surfaced in AI responses. Content Audit. It highlights areas where your pages could provide stronger topical coverage, clearer structure, or more useful information, making them more likely to be referenced by AI models. One drawback, however, is that OpenLens doesn’t provide citation analysis at the individual prompt level. However, it doesn’t tell you which specific prompts triggered each citation or how your citations vary across individual queries, as many other AI visibility tools do. This means you can have a holistic view of your overall performance in organic and AI-driven search. Plans & pricing Custom pricing (no public information regarding its plans) Final Verdict LLM answers are highly personalized and volatile. And until ChatGPT and Co give us real user prompt data, AI visibility monitoring will always be a guessing game. No tool today can show you a perfectly accurate picture of your brand’s presence in AI search. But they can help you understand what LLMs reward, which sources they trust, and where your content or authority is falling short. Use these insights to guide your GEO, content, and digital PR strategy — not as absolute truth, but as a strategic compass. If you’d rather have an expert do it for you, explore our AI Search Optimization services . We’ll audit your current AI visibility, uncover the gaps holding you back, and make the necessary improvements. FAQs What is AI visibility tracking? AI visibility tracking is monitoring how often, and how, your brand appears in answers from AI platforms like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, and Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode. Unlike traditional rank tracking, there’s no “position one” to chase. Instead, you run a fixed set of prompts on a schedule. Then you measure how often you’re mentioned, which of your pages get cited, how AI describes you, and how you stack up against competitors. How do you track and measure AI visibility? You track AI visibility by building a set of prompts your buyers would realistically ask, running them across each AI platform repeatedly, and logging the results. Take your prompts from sales calls, support tickets, and Reddit threads, not just a tool’s auto-generated suggestions. The core metrics are: Mention rate: the share of prompts where your brand appears Share of voice: your mentions compared with your competitors’ Citation rate: how often your own URLs are linked as sources Sentiment: whether AI describes you accurately and favorably Pair these with bot traffic analysis in Cloudflare and AI referral traffic in GA4 to see whether visibility turns into visits. Our guide to monitoring brand visibility in AI search walks through the full setup. What is the best AI visibility tracking tool? There’s no single best AI visibility tracking tool. The right pick depends on your team and budget. If you already use an SEO suite, Semrush adds AI tracking without another login. Agencies get the most from OpenLens. If you’re testing on a small budget, Rankscale starts at $20/month. Before you buy, compare three settings: which AI platforms the tool covers, how many prompts you get, and how often it re-runs them. Those settings explain most of the gap between a $20 plan and a $250 one. How can I check my AI visibility score for free? You can check your AI visibility score for free with OpenLens , which has a free-forever plan. Add your website domain, and OpenLens suggests your competitors and core topics. It then runs prompts on ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews and reports your AI visibility score alongside share of voice and total mentions. How accurate are AI visibility tools? AI visibility tools are reliable for spotting trends, like whether you’re gaining or losing ground against a competitor. However, they’re less reliable for showing exactly what a buyer sees, as AI answers are unique to each person. Moreover, some tools query AI models through their APIs, which can return different answers from the ChatGPT or Perplexity apps people actually use. Should I use an AI visibility tool or hire an agency? Use a tool if you have an in-house SEO or content team with time to act on the data. Hire an AI SEO agency if you don’t. A tool shows you where you’re missing from AI answers. It won’t write the content, earn the third-party mentions, or fix the technical issues that get you included. If you hire an agency, be wary of anyone who guarantees ChatGPT rankings or sells monthly reports without a plan to change what they show. Nobody controls what an LLM says. They can only improve the signals it draws on. How do I improve AI visibility once I'm tracking it? Start with the prompts where competitors show up and you don’t, and check which sources the AI cites in those answers. Those cited pages are where you need to earn a mention, through AI citation outreach . They might be review sites, listicles, Reddit threads, or industry publications. On your own site, open each section with a direct one- or two-sentence answer that AI can quote cleanly. Also make sure your robots.txt doesn’t block the crawlers AI platforms use to fetch pages, such as OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot.
